chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Khirash narrated to us, he said: My master Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Modesty, all of it is good. - Meaning that modesty restrains the one with religion and the one without religion from the ugly (vices), so it is the collection of all that is beautiful (virtues) -.

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Modesty or shyness, a key ethical virtue

ai.seo_question: What is the comprehensive benefit of modesty in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith defines modesty (*al-haya'*) as an all-encompassing virtue that restrains both the religious and the non-religious from vice. It highlights modesty as the foundational character trait that naturally prevents moral corruption, thereby serving as the source of all other beauties in conduct.

en.basel-kadem: 91.	We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ahmad al-Tabari, that he said: We were told by Abu Sa’eed, that he said: We were told by Khirash, that he said: We were told by my master, Anas bin Malik, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:

The one who fasts a day voluntarily, if he is given the amount of what fills the earth with gold, his reward will not be fulfilled as compared to that of the Day of Reckoning. It means that the reward for fasting is not estimated like how one good deed is estimated by ten the likes of it. The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, said: All the deeds of the son of Adam are by ten the likes of them until seven hundred the likes of, except for patience, for indeed, it is for Me, and I will reward for it. Thus, the reward for patience is concealed in the Knowledge of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, and patience is fasting.
